title: Arras for Godot 4: Your Playthrough Woven Into a Tapestry
shortText: Your playthrough woven into a Bayeux style tapestry in Godot 4: 48 scenes drawn in code, 6 dye sets, PNG export.
html:
Arras for Godot 4: your playthrough, woven into a tapestry

Arras is a Godot 4.7 addon that turns what a player did into a Bayeux style embroidered hanging they can open and scroll. Each act of the playthrough becomes one woven panel: figures, a border, a ground and a stitched Latin inscription that names the act in your own words. It ships 48 scenes over 16 figures, 12 props (ships, halls, castles, trees, a feast table, a comet), 10 border registers, 5 grounds and 6 dye sets, and every figure, letter and stitch is drawn at runtime by code. No image file ships. Royalty free in your games. A free lite with 12 of the scenes is on this page.

var chronicle := ArrasChronicle.new()
chronicle.weave("The oath at Roven")          # the scene is read from the words: an oath
chronicle.weave("Crossing the narrow sea")    # a voyage
chronicle.weave("Mournhold", "siege")         # or name the scene yourself

var hanging := ArrasHanging.new()             # a Control: scroll it with keys, wheel or mouse
hanging.chronicle = chronicle
add_child(hanging)

What is in it

  • ArrasChronicle, the record you keep with your save. weave(title) reads the title for the scene it describes (every scene has a word list; whole words, so "burn" matches "burned" but never a name like "Burnley") and freezes the act: scene, border, ground and seed. A later version can never re weave a saved hanging. to_dict() and from_dict() for your own save file, or keep it as a .tres.
  • ArrasHanging, the whole hanging as a scrollable Control on a carved rod with a fringed hem. Only the panels near the view are stitched, so a 40 act hanging costs what four panels cost. The borders run on from panel to panel. save_png() writes the hanging as one strip.
  • ArrasPanel, one woven panel anywhere in a 2D scene: a chapter card, an ending screen, a quest log entry. Scene, title, dye set, border and ground are inspector properties. save_png() included.
  • 48 ready scenes, one .tscn each: the council, the oath, the crowning, the battle, the siege, the duel, the ambush, the burning, the crossing, the landing, the storm, the bridge, the harbour market, the shipwrights, the forge, the ploughing, the fair, the feast, the wedding, the blessing of the fleet, the healing, the pilgrimage, the vigil, the hunt, the watch, the homecoming, the exile, the omen, the writing, the prophecy, the treaty, the finding, the letter, the wyrm, the lair, the taming, the flight, the muster, the beacon and more.
  • The lettering is stitched, not typed. Twenty three Romanesque capitals laid as thread, the way the tapestry spells: J becomes I, U becomes V, W becomes VV.
  • 6 dye sets: Bayeux, Northlands, Harvest, Verdigris, Crownlands and Ashland. Colour is arbitrary within a set, as on the real thing; a figure is told apart by its pose and what it carries.
  • A demo: a fourteen act playthrough on a hall wall, a gallery of every scene, weave the next act, change the dyes, save a PNG.

How it is drawn

Every outline is a stem stitch: short laps slanted against the line, each tinted by how it faces the light. Every fill is laid and couched work: a flat wool with a fine grain and a lattice of tacks. The linen weave runs on through faces and hands. Each panel is stitched once into a supersampled texture, so threads stay smooth under every renderer. A panel takes about 20 to 50 ms to stitch on the test machine; after that scrolling a 40-act hanging end to end measured a median frame of under 3 ms with vsync off, on both renderers.

Both renderers, tested

All 48 scenes photographed under Forward+ and Compatibility (the renderer web exports use): 48 + 48 frames, zero engine errors, every scene measured as a distinct picture against a bare panel. Installed from the shipped zip into a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, where the panel, the shipped scene files, a chronicle in a hanging, PNG export, save and load, the word reading of every scene and all six dye sets were run under both renderers. Mobile was run too. Older Godot 4 versions were not run, so they are not claimed.

Free lite on this page

Arras Lite is free (MIT): 12 of the 48 scenes (the council, the battle, the siege, the crossing, the storm, the fair, the feast, the pilgrimage, the errand, the hunt, the omen, the wyrm) with the same panel, hanging, chronicle, dye sets and demo.

Install

Copy addons/arras into your project and keep it at that path. No plugin to enable.

Licence

Royalty free in your games, commercial use, no credit required. Use the hangings, and the PNG files you or your players export, in your games, trailers and store pages; let players share what their playthrough wove. You may not resell or redistribute the files or a collection of exported panels as a pack or image collection. Plain language LICENSE.txt included.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the scripts, shader and scenes were written with AI, the Latin formulae and sample act titles too, and every figure and stitch is drawn by that code at runtime from an authored corpus of joints and strokes. The cover was rendered by the pack itself.
